name: Groundnut
description: Premier oilseed and food legume crop in India, widely cultivated in Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Rajasthan. Characterized by geocarpic pod development (pegging underground). Sensitive to calcium deficiency (pops) and Tikka leaf spot.
climate: Warm tropical climate with moderate and evenly distributed rainfall during growing season and dry weather at harvest.

soil.drainage_requirement: Excellent aeration and friability needed in top 10 cm of soil to facilitate easy peg penetration. Heavy compacted clay soils severely restrict pegging and pod harvesting.
soil.organic_matter_requirement: Moderate (>0.5% OC); apply 10 tonnes/ha FYM or 2.5 tonnes vermicompost.

planting_seasons: Kharif (June - July sowing with monsoon arrival)
Rabi / Summer (November - January sowing under irrigation)
seed_rate_per_ha: 120-140 kg/ha kernels for bunch types; 100-110 kg/ha for spreading types.

growth_stages.description: Kernel germination, taproot growth, and nodule initiation by Rhizobium bacteria.
Copious yellow self-pollinating flowers appear in leaf axils.
critical_activities: Intercultivation and light weeding before pegs start forming
Do NOT disturb soil after peg entry begins

growth_stages.description: Gynophores (pegs) elongate downward, penetrate topsoil 3-5 cm, and swell horizontally into pods.
critical_activities: Crucial Gypsum application @ 400-500 kg/ha at pegging (supplies Calcium for shell hardening)
Ensure soil moisture to keep topsoil soft

growth_stages.description: Kernel oil accumulation, shell inner lining turns dark brown to black.
critical_activities: Light irrigation to soften soil 2 days before pulling
Avoid excessive moisture to prevent in-situ seed germination
vulnerabilities: Aflatoxin contamination (Aspergillus flavus) due to late season moisture stress or delay in post-harvest drying

nutrients.basal_application: Full NPK at sowing (legume fixes atmospheric N via root nodules).
top_dressing_schedule: Crucial: Apply Gypsum @ 400 kg/ha at 40-45 DAS along the row zone and earth up slightly.
micronutrient_requirements: Ferrous sulphate 1% foliar spray with 0.1% citric acid against lime-induced iron chlorosis

harvesting.duration_days: 100-115 days for bunch varieties; 120-135 days for semi-spreading varieties
maturity_indices: Yellowing and shedding of older leaves
Inner surface of shell turns dark blackish brown
Kernels attain typical pink/rose color and detach easily
harvesting.harvesting_method: Pull entire plants manually or groundnut digger; invert plants in field for sun drying.
harvesting.average_yield_per_ha: 2.0 - 2.8 tonnes/ha dry pods under irrigated conditions
harvesting.post_harvest_care: Dry pods to 8% moisture content before bagging to eliminate Aspergillus flavus and aflatoxin risk.
